stories.title: Israeli Airstrikes Kill At Least 9 in Southern Lebanon Village
stories.summary: Israel's air force carried out two airstrikes early Monday on Kfar Rumman, a village in southern Lebanon, killing at least nine people and wounding 13, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. One strike hit a residential building, killing eight people including a child and two women, while a separate strike on a car killed a paramedic with a Lebanese scout association. Israel's military said the strikes targeted Hezbollah militants transporting weapons into the village, in response to two Hezbollah drone attacks on Israeli troops earlier that day. The attack marks one of the most serious escalations since a truce between Israel and Hezbollah took hold more than two months ago.

stories.title: Canada's Retaliatory Tariffs on $20 Billion of U.S. Goods Take Effect
stories.summary: Canada's counter-tariffs on more than 700 U.S. products took effect at 12:01 a.m. on September 8, matching roughly C$27.6 billion (about $20 billion) in new duties the United States imposed on Canadian goods after trade talks collapsed on August 22. The tariffs range from 15% to 50% and cover steel, aluminum, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper and electronics, with Canada doubling its own steel and aluminum duties to 50% to match U.S. levies on those products. Ottawa paired the move with a C$7.5 billion aid package to support affected businesses and workers. No new trade talks have resumed between the two countries since negotiations broke down.

stories.title: Indian Spacetech Startup Pixxel Raises $100 Million in Series C Funding
stories.summary: Pixxel, an Indian planetary infrastructure company, closed a $100 million Series C round co-led by Temasek and Seraphim Space, with new backers 360 ONE Asset and IMM Investment joining existing investors including Google and Radical Ventures. The round, India's largest-ever spacetech fundraise, brings Pixxel's total capital raised to $195 million and will fund new hyperspectral and optical-imaging satellites, its Aurora Earth-intelligence software, sovereign observation systems and a high-rate satellite manufacturing facility called Gigapixxel. Pixxel currently operates six Firefly satellites forming what it says is the world's highest-resolution commercial hyperspectral constellation, and holds contracts with NASA and the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office. The company has also been selected to lead a 12-satellite public-private Earth observation constellation for India's IN-SPACe space agency.

stories.title: Apple Set to Unveil First Foldable iPhone at September 9 Launch Event
stories.summary: Apple is expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone, reportedly called the iPhone Ultra, at a September 9 event that will mark new CEO John Ternus's debut product launch since succeeding Tim Cook. The device is rumored to cost more than $2,000, feature a 5.5-inch cover display that expands to 7.8 inches when unfolded, and skip Face ID in favor of a side-mounted Touch ID button. Apple is also expected to refresh the non-folding iPhone 18 Pro line and HomePod speakers, and, according to leaks found in a macOS preview build, introduce AirPods with built-in low-resolution cameras that feed its Siri-linked Visual Intelligence feature.

stories.title: Antarctica Gained a Record 695 Billion Tons of Ice, Study Finds
stories.summary: A study published in Nature found that East Antarctica gained a record 695 billion tons of ice between 2021 and 2023, the largest increase recorded by GRACE satellites, temporarily slowing the continent's long-term ice loss. Researchers traced the cause to sustained warming in the tropical ocean thousands of miles away, which altered atmospheric circulation and funneled moisture toward Antarctica, triggering exceptionally heavy snowfall. The researchers emphasized that the gain was temporary and does not reverse Antarctica's long-term decline, which has averaged about 140.5 billion tons of ice lost per year over the past two decades.
